title: Quantization Profile Library — Production Release Checklist (Opt-in, Route-level)
body:
Doc purpose
- This is the step-by-step release checklist for enabling the Quantization Profile Library in production as an opt-in, route-level feature.
- Scope: migrations, config/feature flags, staged canary rollout, and verification/rollback steps across hosted + dedicated.
- Non-goal: making profiles default-on. Baseline behavior must be unchanged when feature is off.

Owners / oncall roles (fill before running)
- Release driver (Eng Releases): ____________________ (default: Connor O’Brien)
- Platform control plane / routing: ____________________ (default: Ethan Park / Mina Haddad)
- Runtime: ____________________ (default: Noah Patel)
- Observability: ____________________ (default: Aisha Bello / Logan Wright)
- Console: ____________________ (default: Chloe Martin)
- Applied ML eval signoff: ____________________ (default: Arjun Desai / Selene Huang)

Change summary (what is being turned on)
- New route config field: quantization_profile_ref (nullable / default)
- Control plane endpoints + policy evaluation resolves quant profile deterministically, with compatibility checks and fallback to baseline
- Runtime loads profile artifacts when resolved and emits metrics/log annotations (quant_profile_id, resolution outcome)
- Console UI adds route-level toggle + change history (RBAC gated)
- Global kill-switch disables all quant profiles (even if configured on routes)

Release principles / safety invariants
- Determinism: same route config + model version + region/tier => same resolved profile ref; resolution outcome is logged.
- Safety fallback: if incompatible, fail “closed” to baseline precision (do not 4xx customer traffic by default).
- Kill-switch precedence: global kill-switch overrides all route-level enablement.
- Auditability: all enable/disable and profile ref changes produce structured audit events.

Pre-flight (T-3 to T-1 days)
[ ] Confirm all required PRs are merged to the production release branch (or tagged):
    - Migration: redwood/pr-18605
    - Control plane endpoints: redwood/pr-18445
    - Kill-switch: redwood/pr-18488
    - Runtime integration + metrics: redwood/pr-18463, redwood/pr-18555
    - Compatibility guardrails: redwood/pr-18427 (+ hotfix pr-18531 if still applicable)
    - Console backend + changelog: redwood/pr-18496, redwood/pr-18566
    - E2E tests: redwood/pr-18583
    - Perf canary: perf-canary/pr-18520

[ ] Confirm model registry has at least one “known-good” published profile for beta models (Applied ML to confirm) and that any blocked profiles are marked deprecated/disabled.
[ ] Confirm the compatibility matrix doc is up to date (or at least internally shareable) for support/oncall.
[ ] Confirm alerting + dashboards exist and are visible to oncall:
    - enabled_routes_count / enabled_requests_rate
    - fallback_rate (applied vs fallback vs disabled)
    - p95 decode latency delta (baseline vs enabled) per route/model/region
    - 5xx/4xx error rates for quantization endpoints and registry metadata fetch
    - registry metadata fetch QPS/cache hit rate

[ ] Security/RBAC readiness:
    - Confirm which roles can change route quant settings in Console/API (Naomi Feldman to sign off)
    - Confirm audit log export includes quant_profile_id + route_id + actor + diff (Kevin Osei aware)

[ ] Comms:
    - Draft internal release note + oncall heads-up
    - Identify design partner routes for initial canary (PM/CS to provide route IDs)

Environment sequencing
- dev -> staging -> perf-canary -> prod canary (internal) -> prod limited beta (design partners) -> widen (as approved)

STAGING release checklist
1) Deploy control plane + runtime + console backend changes to staging
[ ] Control plane deploy complete
[ ] Runtime deploy complete
[ ] Console backend deploy complete

2) Run migrations (staging)
[ ] Apply DB/config migration for quantization_profile_ref field (ref: pr-18605)
    - Verify backward-compatible serialization (older clients can read configs)
    - Verify route config read/write still works with quant field absent

3) Feature flags / config toggles (staging)
[ ] Global kill-switch default state: OFF (meaning profiles allowed if enabled) in staging
[ ] Feature gate for “quant profiles route config” enabled for internal test tenants only
[ ] Console toggle visible only to allowed RBAC group(s)

4) Staging verification tests
API + policy resolution
[ ] Create a test route with quantization_profile_ref="default" => expect baseline
[ ] Create a test route with quantization_profile_ref="<valid profile id>" => expect applied
[ ] Create a test route with incompatible profile (wrong GPU class / seq len cap) => expect fallback to baseline
[ ] Confirm policy engine returns resolved profile ref deterministically across repeated requests

Runtime + observability
[ ] Confirm request logs/traces include:
    - quant_profile_id
    - quant_profile_resolution (applied|fallback|disabled)
    - model_id / model_variant / route_id
[ ] Confirm metrics are emitted and dashboards populate in staging

Console workflow
[ ] Enable quant profile via Console on a staging route
[ ] Confirm warning text appears for “experimental / quality risk” when applicable
[ ] Confirm audit/change history shows the diff and actor

Perf / cost sanity
[ ] Run a short perf suite sample (10–15 min) comparing baseline vs enabled on 1–2 target models
[ ] Confirm no p95 latency regression > agreed threshold for staging (use perf-canary thresholds as guidance)

PERF-CANARY checklist (pre-prod)
[ ] Merge/verify perf-canary scenarios pr-18520 deployed
[ ] Run baseline vs quant scenario pack:
    - Decode p95 delta within threshold
    - No sustained GPU OOMs
    - Fallback rate remains near 0 for compatible scenarios
[ ] Confirm alert routes are configured to page eng-releases + runtime on regression

PRODUCTION rollout checklist (day-of)
0) Go/no-go gates (must be checked before touching prod)
[ ] Applied ML signoff that selected beta profiles passed required eval suites (per regression thresholds doc)
[ ] SRE/Oncall aware of rollback procedure (link in runbook)
[ ] All required dashboards accessible + alerting live
[ ] Kill-switch verified functioning in staging within last 7 days

1) Deploy code to production (no behavior change expected yet)
[ ] Deploy control plane / routing
[ ] Deploy runtime
[ ] Deploy Console backend (UI may remain gated)

2) Run migrations (prod)
[ ] Apply config/DB migration for quantization_profile_ref
    - Verify migration is safe under mixed-version services
    - Verify no increase in route config read errors

3) Configure flags / allowlists (prod)
Target state for initial prod phase:
- Kill-switch: ON for first 10–30 minutes post-deploy while we validate “no accidental apply” (optional safety move)
- Route-level enablement: allowlisted to internal tenant + 1 design partner (or internal only)

Checklist
[ ] Turn ON kill-switch (optional safety hold) and confirm it propagates to:
    - routing/policy
    - runtime
    - console UI warnings (if applicable)
[ ] Confirm that with kill-switch ON, even explicitly enabled routes resolve to disabled/fallback
[ ] Turn OFF kill-switch when ready to begin canary

4) Prod canary plan (recommended)
Phase A: internal tenant only
[ ] Select 1 internal route (low business impact) on a supported model
[ ] Enable quantization_profile_ref to a specific versioned profile id (avoid “recommended/latest” aliases for beta)
[ ] Send synthetic traffic + a small amount of real traffic (if applicable)
[ ] Monitor for 30–60 minutes:
    - fallback_rate < 0.5% (unless expected due to mixed GPU pool)
    - p95 latency delta within agreed SLO budget
    - error rate unchanged
    - registry metadata fetch QPS stable; cache hit high

Phase B: design partner (1% traffic)
[ ] Confirm design partner route IDs + contact channel for rapid rollback
[ ] Enable on 1 route only
[ ] Use routing policy / traffic splitting (if supported) to start at 1% for 30–60 minutes
[ ] Increase to 10% if clean; hold at 10% for at least 2 hours
[ ] Increase to 50–100% only with explicit PM + SRE approval

5) Verification checklist (prod)
Functional
[ ] For an enabled request id, confirm quant_profile_id is present in logs/traces and resolution is “applied”
[ ] Confirm a forced-incompatible configuration results in fallback (not request failure) and emits a clear reason code

Audit / compliance
[ ] Confirm audit events are generated for:
    - enable/disable toggle
    - profile id change
    - kill-switch toggle
[ ] Confirm audit log exporter includes required fields (INT-9170 follow-up if missing)

Performance / reliability
[ ] Confirm no statistically meaningful regression in p95/p99 latency at route level
[ ] Confirm no spike in 5xx attributable to profile metadata fetch (watch for thundering herd)
[ ] Confirm no increase in GPU memory OOM / evictions on the enabled pool

6) Rollback criteria (explicit)
Immediate rollback if ANY:
- sustained 5xx increase attributable to quant profile path > +0.2% absolute over baseline for 10 minutes
- p95 decode latency regression > threshold (per canary pack) for 15 minutes
- fallback_rate > 5% on a route expected to be fully compatible (indicates compatibility mismatch or mixed pool)
- quality guardrail alert triggers (Applied ML policy) for a beta profile

Rollback actions (in order)
1) Disable at route level (fastest, least blast radius)
[ ] Set quantization_profile_ref="default" for impacted route(s)
[ ] Confirm within 5–10 minutes: applied->disabled transitions in metrics

2) If multiple routes impacted or unclear scope: turn ON global kill-switch
[ ] Toggle kill-switch ON
[ ] Confirm applied rate drops to ~0 across tenants/regions

3) If kill-switch does not arrest impact: revert deployment / roll back to prior stable versions
[ ] Follow standard rollback train procedure

4) Post-rollback verification
[ ] Confirm p95 latency and 5xx return to baseline
[ ] Confirm audit logs reflect all changes and actor

Post-release (T+1 day)
[ ] Write a short release summary in #eng-releases:
    - what was enabled (routes/tenants)
    - observed deltas (cost/token, latency)
    - issues encountered + mitigation
    - next widening step proposal

[ ] File follow-ups:
    - any compatibility matrix gaps (docs)
    - any confusing Console error messages (console/backend)
    - any missing metrics panels / alert tuning (obs)
